title: Project Blueprint: measuring every organ and reversing biological age
summary: Bryan's 2021 launch essay for Project Blueprint: measure all 70+ organs, reverse each one's biological age using only RCT-backed interventions, and let the body's biomarker data decide diet and habits instead of his conscious mind. It lists early results (HRV, fitness, biomarkers) and frames Blueprint as a transferable, self-improving system.

principles.text: Measure every organ, then maximally reverse each one's quantified biological age.
principles.quote: aims to measure all 70+ organs of my body and then maximally reverse the quantified biological age of each.

principles.text: Let biomarker data, not the conscious mind, decide what to eat; remove willpower from the loop.
principles.quote: my body generates the grocery shopping list, communicating their needs through the regular measurement of hundreds of biomarkers.

principles.text: Evidence-based only: no anecdotes, no copying others. Pair each marker with an age reference range and RCT-backed interventions.
principles.quote: In our efforts, we never act on anecdotes. We never do something because others do it.

principles.text: The measurement and intervention system matters more than any specific diet; it should self-improve and become transferable.
principles.quote: It's not as important to assess what I eat as the measurement and intervention system we’ve built to output recommendations.

principles.text: Extremes can backfire: one meal a day pushed body fat under 3%; three meals plus a 10-16 hour daily fast restored 6%.
principles.quote: my one meal a day experiment (that interested me due to its convenience and was not devised by my team) dropped my body fat to under 3%, which is too low.

principles.text: No magic pill is coming; peak wellness is hard work. Reversing biological age more than 1 year per year would signal aging escape velocity.
principles.quote: As for the magic pill, it appears that for the foreseeable future, achieving and maintaining peak wellness is just going to be a lot of really hard work.
